title: Average of Levels in Binary Tree
summary: Return the average value of the nodes on each level of a binary tree, from the top level down.

tests.explain: Level 1 is just 4. Level 2 averages (7 + 9) / 2 = 8. Level 3 averages (10 + 2 + 6) / 3 = 6.
(1 + 2) / 2 = 1.5: averages don't have to be whole numbers.
An empty tree has no levels, so the result is an empty array.

hints: Handle the tree one level at a time. What do you need to know about a level to compute its average?
Use a queue. At the start of each level, the nodes waiting in the queue are exactly that level: remember how many there are.
Dequeue that many nodes, adding up their values and enqueuing their children, then push sum / size.

complexity.time: O(n): every node is enqueued and dequeued once
complexity.space: O(w) for the queue, where w is the widest level (up to n / 2)
